old: Jubilees 4:24 — *he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* the witness-to-the-generations role behind Jasher 3:31, where Enoch's last day teaching bids all men serve Yahuah and walk in his ways.
new: Jasher 3:31 — *he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives.* Enoch's last day of teaching before he was taken is the witness Jubilees says he was set apart to bear.

old: Genesis 6:13 — *And Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.* Jasher 5:25 carries the canon's end-of-all-flesh decree nearly word for word.
new: Jasher 5:25 — *The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds.* Jasher gives the decree of Genesis 6:13 to Noah nearly word for word before the command to build the ark.

old: Jubilees 5:23 — *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* Jubilees keeps the same fountains-of-the-deep that Jasher 6:14 reports, the patriarchal record self-linked.
new: Jasher 6:14 — *all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.* Jubilees 5:24 counts the same fountains and flood-gates Jasher reports being opened.

old: *a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested* (Jasher 6:33) — almost verbatim with Genesis 8:1, the ruach quieting the deep.
new: Jasher 6:33 — *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.* Jasher binds the wind, the stilling of the waters, and the resting of the ark into the one moment Genesis 8:1 describes.

old: Genesis 8:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) smelled a sweet savour; and Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake; for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.* The mercy that follows Noah's altar in Jasher 6:41, the I-will-not-again of the covenant.
new: Jasher 6:41 — *they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons.* The blessing on Noah's house at the going out from the ark is the mercy Genesis 8:21 records Yahuah (LORD) resolving in his heart.

old: Jubilees 6:5 — *And you, increase you and multiply upon the earth, and become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it.* Jubilees keeps the same multiply-and-be-a-blessing word that Jasher 6:42 carries, the patriarchal record self-linked.
new: Jasher 6:42 — *Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth.* Jubilees 6:5 carries the same charge to multiply and be a blessing that Jasher gives Noah's sons at the ark.

old: Matthew 2:1 — *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem.* The wise-men-from-the-east-at-a-royal-birth motif Jasher gives Abram is carried into the Messiah's nativity.
new: Jasher 8:2 — *behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens.* The star Nimrod's wise men read at Abram's birth is answered by the star Herod's wise men follow at the birth of Yahusha (Jesus).

old: Acts 7:4 — *Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell* — the very Ur-Casdim-to-Haran-to-Canaan route Terah's household travels in Jasher 13:1.
new: Jasher 13:1 — *went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan.* Terah's household leaving Ur for Canaan and stopping in Haran is the route Stephen gives in Acts 7:4.

old: Genesis 15:5 — *And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be* — the seed-like-the-stars promise Yahuah binds to keeping his commandments in Jasher 13:4.
new: Jasher 13:4 — *I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven.* The seed numbered like the stars in Genesis 15:5 is spoken in Jasher together with the call to keep his commandments.

old: Genesis 12:7 — *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), who appeared unto him* — the same land-to-your-seed word Yahuah speaks at Abram's entry into Canaan in Jasher 13:7.
new: Jasher 13:7 — *This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever.* Yahuah (the Lord) appearing to Abram on his entry into Canaan and giving the land to his seed is the word of Genesis 12:7.

old: Genesis 13:15 — *For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever* — the all-the-lands-which-you-see inheritance forever of Jasher 13:7.
new: Jasher 13:7 — *I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* All the land Abram sees given to his seed forever is the word of Genesis 13:15 spoken in Jasher at his entry into Canaan.

old: Genesis 12:3 — *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed* — the families-of-the-earth blessing Jasher 13:23 carries verbatim.
new: Jasher 13:23 — *in you shall the families of the earth be blessed.* The blessing on all families of the earth from Genesis 12:3 is kept in Jasher's recall of Abram's call in Haran.

old: Jubilees 13:29 — *I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre.* Jubilees renders Abram's refusal in Jasher 16:16 with the same thread-to-shoe-latchet oath.
new: Jasher 16:16 — *I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread.* Abram's oath to take nothing of Sodom's spoil is the same thread and shoe-latchet refusal Jubilees 13:29 records.

old: Genesis 21:8 — *And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.* Jasher 21:4 retells the canon's great weaning feast verbatim in substance.
new: Jasher 21:4 — *Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.* Jasher retells the great weaning feast of Genesis 21:8 and then names the guests who came to it.

old: Jubilees 19:11 — *And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah. And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.* The same Keturah-and-six-sons scene in the parallel patriarchal record beside Jasher 25:2.
new: Jasher 25:2 — *she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons.* Keturah's six sons in Jasher stand beside Jubilees 19:11, which records Abraham taking her as his third wife.

old: *there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city* (Jasher 34:23) — the oath of total destruction behind *took each man his sword... and slew all the males* (34:25); the fierceness Jacob will curse.
new: Jasher 34:23 — *by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.* The oath Simeon and Levi swear in Jasher is carried out in the slaughter of Genesis 34:25.

old: Deuteronomy 32:30 — *How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?* The Song of Moses names the same one-chasing-a-thousand measure of Jasher 38:50 and ties it to the Rock's hand, not mere strength.
new: Jasher 38:50 — *one of them would pursue a thousand, and two of them would not flee from ten thousand.* The one who chases a thousand in Deuteronomy 32:30 is the measure Jasher gives the men of Sarton before the sons of Jacob slay them.

old: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.* Judah seizing the fallen swords and slaying twenty upon the wall is the hand-on-the-enemies'-neck the blessing foretells.
new: Jasher 39:34 — *Judah took the swords which had fallen from their hands, and Judah fought with them.* Yahudah (Judah) slaying twenty men with their own fallen swords is the hand in the neck of his enemies that Genesis 49:8 foretells.

old: Genesis 39:5 — *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* The blessing-of-Potiphar's-house in Jasher 44:12 is this verse retold.
new: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* Jasher retells Genesis 39:5, where Potiphar's whole house is blessed for Joseph's sake.

old: *Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph* (Jasher 44:12) — the blessing-for-his-sake of 39:5 kept whole; where the favoured dwells, the blessing overflows.
new: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man.* Jasher keeps the blessing on Potiphar's house for Joseph's sake whole beside Genesis 39:5.

old: Jubilees 39:9 — *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* The live Jubilees text holds the same garment-in-her-hands flight as Jasher 44:54.
new: Jasher 44:54 — *Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out.* The garment left in Potiphar's wife's hand as Joseph flees is kept by Jubilees 39:9 as well.

old: Jasher locates Tamar's lineage in Shem's line — *Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem.* Shemitic by blood; the framework reads the four women as seed-preservation markers within or adjacent to the covenant body.
new: Jasher 45:23 — *took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* Jasher places Tamar in the house of Shem, so the Thamar of Matthew 1:3 is a daughter of the kept line, not a Canaanite.

old: Genesis 40:19 — *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.* the hanging-on-a-tree verdict Joseph speaks in Jasher 46:14.
new: Jasher 46:14 — *within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree.* Joseph's verdict that the baker will hang on a tree is the word of Genesis 40:19.

old: Genesis 26:3 — *Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;* The land-for-the-seed oath Isaac repeats in Jasher 47:7 is the word Yahuah first spoke directly to him.
new: Jasher 47:7 — *To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways.* Isaac hands Jacob the land oath Yahuah (the Lord) spoke to him in Genesis 26:3, with the keeping of his statutes attached.

old: Genesis 42:6 — *And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.* Joseph's whole apparatus of statutes in Jasher 50:37 'that he might know when his brethren should come' culminates in this bowing — the dream fulfilled.
new: Jasher 50:37 — *in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn.* Joseph's statutes for the corn sale are laid so that the bowing of his brethren in Genesis 42:6 comes before his own face.

old: Jubilees 45:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* Jubilees dates the same going-out-from-Canaan that Jasher 55:5 narrates from Beersheba into Goshen.
new: Jasher 55:5 — *he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart.* Jacob's going down from Beersheba to Egypt is the journey Jubilees 45:1 dates to the new moon of the fourth month.

old: Genesis 46:29 — *And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.* The fall-upon-the-neck embrace of Jasher 55:15 is Genesis verbatim in substance.
new: Jasher 55:15 — *Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him.* Jacob falling on Joseph's neck in Jasher is the meeting in Goshen of Genesis 46:29.

old: Genesis 46:30 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.* Jacob's now-let-me-die in Jasher 55:16 is the same word — the father content having seen his living son.
new: Jasher 55:16 — *Now I will die cheerfully after I have seen your face.* Jacob's word on seeing Joseph alive, the same word Genesis 46:30 gives him.

old: Genesis 47:6 — *The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.* Pharaoh's best-of-the-land grant in Jasher 55:22 is the same decree.
new: Jasher 55:22 — *Place your father and brethren in the best part of the land.* Pharaoh's grant, the same decree as Genesis 47:6.

old: Genesis 49:29 — *And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,* Jacob's charge to bury him at Machpelah in Jasher 56:3 is the Genesis charge verbatim in substance.
new: Jasher 56:3 — *bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron.* Jacob's burial charge, with the promise that Elohim (God) will visit them and bring them back.

old: Jasher 56:9 — *Only teach your sons the bow and all the weapons of war, in order that they may fight the battles of their brother who will rule over his enemies* — Jasher’s Judah-and-the-bow tradition stands behind Yahudah’s counsel to bend the bow in Jubilees 38:1.
new: Jasher 56:9 — *Only teach your sons the bow and all the weapons of war.* Jacob's deathbed charge to Yahudah (Judah), the bow against Esau's house that Jubilees 38:1 also remembers.

old: Hebrews 11:22 — *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* The bringing-out-of-Egypt Jacob foresees in Jasher 56:21 is the very departing Joseph foretold by faith over his bones.
new: Jasher 56:21 — *bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers.* Jacob foresees the departing Joseph will foretell over his bones in Hebrews 11:22.

old: Exodus 1:5 — *And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.* Exodus echoes the same seventy-from-the-loins count that closes Jasher's roll in 59:19.
new: Jasher 59:19 — *all the souls that went forth from the loins of Jacob, were seventy souls.* The seventy Exodus 1:5 counts, the household as it stood going down into Egypt.

old: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Joseph's evil-meant-for-good is the same reading Jasher 63:7 gives the bondage itself.
new: Jasher 63:7 — *to benefit them in their latter days.* The bondage itself named as from Yahuah (the Lord) and for their good, as Joseph said of his brothers' evil.

old: The Mosheh-parent narrative — Amram and Yochaved (Jochebed) — the deliverer-preserved-through-the-slaughter prototype.
new: Jasher 67:1 — *There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi.* The deliverer's story opens with his father in Egypt, as Matthew 2:13 opens with Joseph carrying the child there.

old: Jasher 67 walks the Pharaoh-infant-slaughter narrative — *the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).*
new: Jasher 67:3 — *the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Israel.* Miriam named for the bitter days; Herod's Bethlehem is the same hand in a later century.

old: *Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel)* — the same antichrist-pattern Herod walks at Beth-lehem.
new: Jasher 67:4 — *Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Israel.* The decree dated by Aaron's conception; Herod's decree at Bethlehem is the same move against the promised seed.

old: Genesis 36:37 — *And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.* The Torah's Edomite king-list names the same Saul-by-the-river succeeding the same Samlah that Jasher 69:2 records.
new: Jasher 69:2 — *they made him king over them in the place of Samlah.* The Saul of Genesis 36:37, from a city upon the river, and how the children of Esau fetched him.

old: Acts 7:29 — *Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.* Stephen frames the same long exile-before-the-call that Jasher fills with the Cush years, Moses a stranger far from his brethren until the appointed time.
new: Jasher 76:12 — *the period had arrived which he had appointed in the days of old.* The Cush years end on Yahuah's (the Lord's) schedule, the long stretch away from his brethren that Stephen names in Acts 7:29.

old: Exodus 2:22 — *And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.* The same naming of Gershom that Jasher 78:9 records, the stranger-in-a-foreign-land confession word for word.
new: Jasher 78:9 — *he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land.* The naming Exodus 2:22 records, with Jasher adding that the boy was left uncircumcised at Reuel's command.

old: Acts 7:35 — *This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did Elohim (God) send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.* The deliverer-from-Pharaoh's-sword that Eliezer's name marks in Jasher 78:10.
new: Jasher 78:10 — *the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.* Eliezer's name confesses the rescue; Acts 7:35 has the rescued man sent back as deliverer.

old: Exodus 7:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.* The blood-by-the-hand-of-Aaron of Jasher 80:3 is Exodus' own first plague.
new: Jasher 80:3 — *turned all the waters of Egypt into blood, with all their streams and rivers.* The first plague by Aaron's hand, as Exodus 7:19 commands it.

old: Exodus 12:30 — *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.* Pharaoh rising and the houseless-of-the-living of Jasher 80:44 is Exodus' great cry.
new: Jasher 80:44 — *there was not a house in which there was not a corpse.* The night of the firstborn, Exodus 12:30 nearly word for word.

old: Exodus 12:36 — *And Yahuah (LORD) gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.* The substance carried out with the multitude of Jasher 81:2 is the canon's spoiling of Egypt.
new: Jasher 81:2 — *Also a mixed multitude went up with them, and flocks and herds, even much cattle.* What went up out of Egypt, beside the goods Exodus 12:36 says the Egyptians lent them.

old: Exodus 14:13 — *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* Moses' charge in Jasher 81:28 is the canon's stand-still word verbatim in substance.
new: Jasher 81:28 — *Fear not, stand still and see the salvation of Yahuah (the Lord).* Moses' word at the sea, Exodus 14:13 spoken into a people split into divisions.

old: Hebrews 13:5 — *Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.* The New Covenant carries forward the very I-will-not-forsake-thee promise spoken in Jasher 87:4.
new: Jasher 87:4 — *he will not leave you nor forsake you.* The promise to Joshua that Hebrews 13:5 still quotes as his word.

old: Deuteronomy 5:32 — *Ye shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.* Jasher 87:6 repeats the very turn-not-to-the-right-or-left refrain of Moses' charge to keep the way.
new: Jasher 87:6 — *observe all the words of this law, and walk in the way of Yahuah your Elohim.* Moses' last charge, the Deuteronomy 5:32 word to keep the whole law and turn neither right nor left.

old: Deuteronomy 32:50 — *And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people; as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people.* Jasher 87:9 keeps the very gathered-to-your-people-as-Aaron wording.
new: Jasher 87:9 — *be gathered to your people as Aaron your brother was gathered.* The call to Abarim, Deuteronomy 32:50 in Jasher's wording.

old: Joshua 1:2 — *Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The command to rise and pass the Jordan to inherit the land in Jasher 88:2 is Joshua 1:2 verbatim in substance.
new: Jasher 88:2 — *Rise up and pass the Jordan to the land which I have given.* The commission of Joshua 1:2, with the charge to make the children inherit it.

old: Deuteronomy 11:24 — *Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be.* The sole-of-the-foot boundary to Lebanon and the river of Perath in Jasher 88:3 is the inheritance-word Moses already gave.
new: Jasher 88:3 — *Every place upon which the sole of your feet shall tread shall belong to you.* The borders Moses had already read out in Deuteronomy 11:24, Perath being the Euphrates.

old: Joshua 4:19 — *And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho.* The tenth-day-of-the-first-month encampment at Gilgal in Jasher 88:10 matches the canon to the day and the place.
new: Jasher 88:10 — *on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped in Gilgal.* The day and place of Joshua 4:19, the lamb's day, with Passover kept four days on.

old: Joshua 14:1 — *And these are the countries which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), distributed for inheritance to them.* The same Eleazar-Joshua-tribal-heads portioning by lot that Jasher 90:23 records at Shiloh.
new: Jasher 90:23 — *portioned out to the children of Israel by lot in Shiloh.* The division Joshua 14:1 heads, done before Yahuah (the Lord) at the tabernacle door.

old: Joshua 21:43 — *And Yahuah (LORD) gave unto Yashar'el (Israel) all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein.* The sworn-to-the-fathers land-gift that Jasher 90:24 restates as Yahuah giving and Israel possessing.
new: Jasher 90:24 — *they possessed it as Yahuah (the Lord) had spoken to them.* The close of the conquest as Joshua 21:43 gives it, the land given as sworn to the fathers.

old: Matthew 4:10 — *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah thy Elohim (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* As the adversary tempts Abraham aside from the command in Jasher 23:25, so the Messiah turns the same tempter away with the word — the chosen seed will not be drawn aside.
new: Matthew 4:10 — *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* As the adversary tempts Abraham aside from the command in Jasher 23:25, so the Messiah turns the same tempter away with the word — the chosen seed will not be drawn aside.

old: *go to my land and to my birthplace, and take a wife for my son* (Jasher 24:31) — the second half of the charge of 24:4, the bride sought from the covenant family alone, the angel sent before the way.
new: *go to my land and to my birthplace, and take from there a wife for my son* (Jasher 24:31) — the second half of the charge of 24:4, the bride sought from the covenant family alone, the angel sent before the way.

old: *he fled to the house of Eber the son of Shem... and he there continued to learn the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his commandments* (Jasher 29:11) — the flight of 27:43 becomes a schooling in the Torah-walk; the chosen seed keeps the commandments even in exile.
new: *fled to the house of Eber the son of Shem... and he there continued to learn the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his commandments* (Jasher 29:11) — the flight of 27:43 becomes a schooling in the Torah-walk; the chosen seed keeps the commandments even in exile.

old: *may the El Shaddai (Almighty God) give you mercy before him that he may send Benjamin and Simeon* (Jasher 52:23) — Jacob's blessing of 43:14 kept word-for-heart; the surrender cast on El Shaddai's mercy.
new: *may El Shaddai (the Almighty God) give you mercy before him that he may send Benjamin and Simeon* (Jasher 52:23) — Jacob's blessing of 43:14 kept word-for-heart; the surrender cast on El Shaddai's mercy.

old: *Yahuah will raise up to you and your children a servant... and deliver you... from all affliction* (Jasher 56:21) — Jacob's death-bed hope (49:18) rests on the Deliverer Yahuah promised to raise.
new: *will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant... will deliver you through his hand from all affliction* (Jasher 56:21) — Jacob's death-bed hope (49:18) rests on the Deliverer Yahuah promised to raise.
